story: In 2022, Ferdinand Marcos Jr., son of the dictator ousted in 1986, and Sara Duterte, daughter of the strongman president Rodrigo Duterte, ran together as the "UniTeam" and won by a landslide. The alliance of the two dynasties collapsed within two years. In 2025, Rodrigo Duterte was arrested and flown to The Hague to face charges at the International Criminal Court over his drug war. In 2026, the feud reached the Senate.

After the Supreme Court voided her first impeachment in 2025, new complaints were filed against Vice President Sara Duterte in February 2026, accusing her of misusing about $10 million in confidential funds as education secretary and of threatening to have Marcos assassinated (AFP via NST). The House impeached her, and by May she faced trial in the Senate. Her defence is to point at Marcos. A huge scandal over bogus flood-control projects, in a country battered by typhoons, has drawn mass protests, and 18 former marines claimed they delivered some 805 billion pesos in kickbacks to lawmakers and Marcos himself; Marcos denies it and faces impeachment complaints of his own that have gone nowhere (Asia News Network). The Catholic bishops warned against "selective justice" (UCA News). Duterte, meanwhile, has declared she will run for president in 2028. A Senate conviction would bar her from office for life.
briefing.power: A presidential republic modelled on the US. The president is elected for a single six-year term; the vice president is elected separately and can come from a rival camp. Congress has a House and a 24-member Senate, which tries impeachments.
briefing.holders: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., since 2022; Vice President Sara Duterte.
